data.exact_reserve_text: For the purposes of preparing these Financial Statements, the Managing Agent has adopted its external actuarial consultants' best estimate outcome. In respect of business earned at 31 December 2017, the gross and net reserves, excluding claims handling costs and run-off provision, as at 31 December 2017 total GBP 172.9 million and GBP 125.3 million respectively. During the year there was net claims development improvement of GBP 14.7 million on the 2013 and prior years, GBP 1.9 million on the 2014 year, GBP 2.7 million on the 2015 year and an improvement of GBP 0.5 million on the 2016 year of account.

prior_year_events.impact_description: A reduction in the ultimate gross claims on the primary professional indemnity account drove a reduction in ultimate gross claims.
Increase in the excess layers following the claims review partially offset reductions in the primary account.

data.standardized_narrative: At 1 January 2017 gross claims outstanding were GBP 231.843m. During 2017 the syndicate recorded an overall gross prioryear release of c. GBP 9.29m (4.0% of opening reserves). The movement was driven by favourable development in older years (notably a large reduction in the primary professional indemnity portfolio) partially offset by strengthening in excess layers. The Managing Agent cites a mix of causes including favourable mediation/ADR outcomes, reserve methodology updates and ongoing uncertainty from longrunning complex litigation.
raw_causal_phrases: significant deterioration seen in the claims reserves during 2015
high degree of uncertainty over the outcome of many claims due to their relative stage of development
many of which involve complex litigation over a long period
incorporation of the reserves advised by the independent claims consultants in 2015 and the internal case reserve increases in 2016 led to some distortion in the development patterns
positive developments against expectation have been recognised by LCP in the reserving process

The reduction in ultimate gross claims of GBP 16,233k was driven by a GBP 22,900k reduction to the primary professional indemnity account which was historically the Syndicate's largest portfolio. This was partially offset by a GBP 10,704k increase in the excess layers following the claims review.

a comprehensive review of all outstanding case reserves was conducted by the Claims team to determine the expected probability and severity of a large claim emerging on a case by case basis. This analysis revealed particular classes of business and years of account where the reserves were overly cautious or required strengthening.
data.data_quality_notes: Opening gross claims outstanding taken from Statement of Financial Position (Technical provisions - Claims outstanding) prior year comparative column. Prior year development (gross) taken from the 'Changes for prior years' line in the Technical Provisions reconciliation (gross column). Narrative also reports several 'net' improvements (net of reinsurance) which were not used for the gross PYD figure. Limited line-of-business level gross prior-year movement detail is available (PI primary release and excess-layer strengthening are disclosed); other LOB movements are not quantified gross in the notes. No specific named catastrophe events are cited.
